item.title: Scott Pelley Signs With CAA After Shocking '60 Minutes' Firing
item.description:
Scott Pelley Signs With CAA After Shocking ‘60 Minutes’ Firing

What does a 51-time Emmy winner do after getting fired with no severance and 37 years on the line? He signs with one of Hollywood’s most powerful talent agencies — and makes it clear he is not done.

Scott Pelley has officially signed with Creative Artists Agency (CAA), just weeks after his abrupt and bitter departure from CBS News and “60 Minutes.” The agency confirmed the deal in an Instagram post on Thursday, June 25, 2026, marking the veteran journalist’s first major career move since his exit.

item.title: Pete Buttigieg Breaks Silence on Shocking Hoax Targeting His Family
item.description:
Imagine being briefly separated from your own children because an anonymous stranger told authorities you were a danger to them. That is exactly what happened to Pete Buttigieg, and his decision to speak out is reshaping the conversation around his political future.

The former Transportation Secretary—and a leading potential 2028 Democratic presidential contender—just revealed one of the most disturbing episodes of his public life. And he is, in his own words, “beyond furious.”

item.title: New York Times Under Fire: Two Stories Shaking the Paper
item.description:
The most influential newspaper in America is spending this week investigating itself — and defending its own reporting at the same time. The New York Times, long considered the gold standard of American journalism, is at the center of two very different controversies that have erupted within days of each other.

One questions how the paper covered a politically charged social issue. The other involves one of its own star reporters. Together, they raise a bigger question: what happens when the watchdog becomes the story?

item.title: SCOTUSblog: The Essential Guide to Supreme Court News
item.description:
Here’s a number that stopped a lot of people in 2007: 100,000 page views in a single day — for a blog about the Supreme Court. Not a celebrity scandal, not a sports score. Court opinions.

That blog was SCOTUSblog, and nearly two decades later it remains the single most-trusted independent source for understanding what the U.S. Supreme Court actually does. If you’ve ever wondered how reporters seem to explain a complex ruling within minutes of its release, the answer is often the same: they’re reading SCOTUSblog.

item.title: Fortnite Server Status: The Essential June 25 Downtime Guide
item.description:
Millions of players type the same three words into Google every single day: “is Fortnite down?” On June 25, 2026, that search spiked again as Epic Games took the game offline for scheduled maintenance.

If you booted up your console this morning only to get stuck in an endless lobby, you are not alone. Checking the Fortnite server status has become a daily ritual for one of the world’s most popular games.

item.title: AMBER Alert Explained: The Surprising System That Saved 1,312 Kids
item.description:
What if the buzzing phone in your pocket could be the single difference between a child coming home safe and a tragedy that never ends?

That is exactly what an AMBER Alert is built to do. As of December 31, 2025, 1,312 children have been successfully recovered thanks to the activation of an AMBER Alert in the United States. Behind that number are thousands of ordinary people who simply paid attention to a notification.

item.title: Texas Tech Boom: The Surprising Week That Defined the State
item.description:
What do 20 million escaped honeybees, a federal Tesla probe, and one of the largest tech companies on Earth have in common? In a single week of June 2026, all of them put Texas at the center of the national conversation.

The Lone Star State has long been a magnet for energy, industry, and headlines. But the events unfolding right now reveal something bigger: Texas is quietly becoming the proving ground for the artificial intelligence era.

item.title: Rio Ferdinand's Surprising Second Act: From United Legend to Media Mogul
item.description:
Rio Ferdinand’s Surprising Second Act: From United Legend to Media Mogul

What does a footballer do after 35 years of being governed by a fixture list? If you’re Rio Ferdinand, you build a multi-million pound media empire — and become one of the most quoted voices of the 2026 World Cup along the way.

The Manchester United legend has reinvented himself so thoroughly that his post-playing career may eventually rival his trophy-laden time on the pitch. Here’s how he did it, and why his words still dominate football headlines.

item.title: Schools Under Scrutiny: The Surprising Federal Probes Reshaping US Education
item.description:
Why are American schools suddenly the center of so many federal investigations? In a single day this June, the US Department of Education opened or advanced probes into multiple school districts across the country—and that’s just the headline. From Title IX disputes in Michigan to restroom policy investigations in North Carolina, the conversation around K-12 education has rarely been this charged.

Quick Summary: Federal investigators are scrutinizing US schools over Title IX, restroom access, and athletic eligibility. Meanwhile, an AI arms race is reshaping classrooms, and access policies are tightening from Florida to Michigan. Here’s what’s actually happening—and why it matters for every American family.

item.title: Honda's Stunning Hybrid Pivot Shakes the Auto World
item.description:
Honda just posted its first annual loss as a publicly traded company since 1957 — and that’s only the third-most dramatic Honda headline this week. The automaker is simultaneously recalling more than 880,000 vehicles, fending off an internal coup against its CEO, and pivoting its entire global strategy away from a pure EV future. For an 80-year-old company built on engineering discipline, the past seven days have been chaos.

So what is Honda actually doing — and what does it mean for the millions of Americans who own one of its cars?

item.title: Fraud Losses Hit Record $15.9 Billion: The Surprising 2026 Reality
item.description:
Americans lost a staggering $15.9 billion to fraud in 2025 — a record-shattering figure that exposes just how aggressive, organized, and digitally savvy today’s scammers have become. If you think fraud is somebody else’s problem, the latest numbers from the Federal Trade Commission suggest otherwise.

Key Takeaways

  • Consumer fraud losses hit a record $15.9 billion in 2025, up from $12.5 billion in 2024 (FTC).
  • Investment scams alone accounted for nearly half — $7.9 billion.
  • Imposter scams generated more than 1 million reports and $3.5 billion in losses.
  • The SBA referred 562,000 suspected fraudulent pandemic loans worth $22.2 billion to Treasury for collection in April 2026.
  • Reported fraud losses have surged nearly 430% since 2020.

The scope of fraud in America has shifted dramatically in just five years. What used to be isolated cons targeting the elderly has become a multibillion-dollar industry blending text messages, social media, and impersonation tactics that fool people of every age group. Below, we unpack the numbers — and what they actually mean for your wallet.

item.title: Instagram Plus Unveiled: Essential Features, Price & Why It Matters
item.description:
Instagram Plus Unveiled: Essential Features, Price & Why It Matters

For the first time in its 16-year history, Instagram is asking users to pay to unlock parts of the app. Instagram Plus officially launched globally on June 4, 2026, priced at $3.99 per month, and the social media world is already split between curious early adopters and frustrated regulars who feel core features are being walled off.

Quick Summary

  • What it is: A premium Instagram subscription with 11 exclusive features
  • Price: $3.99/month, rolling out globally on iPhone
  • Focus: Story enhancements and profile customization
  • Availability: iOS first; Android not yet announced
  • The free version of Instagram remains unchanged

What Is Instagram Plus?

Instagram Plus is a premium subscription tier from Meta that unlocks exclusive tools inside the standard Instagram app. According to Meta’s head of product Naomi Gleit and Instagram CEO Adam Mosseri, who confirmed the rollout via video, the subscription is designed for users who want “more control, deeper insights, and premium features.”

item.title: Pokemon GO Fest Chicago 2026: The Ultimate Trainer Guide
item.description:
Pokemon GO Fest Chicago 2026: The Ultimate Trainer Guide

Up to 40,000 trainers per day are descending on Grant Park this weekend — phones charged, Poké Balls stocked, and Pikachu hats firmly in place. Pokemon GO Fest Chicago is back, and it’s bigger than the festival that nearly broke the internet in 2017.

Quick Summary

  • When: June 5–7, 2026 (citywide gameplay began June 4)
  • Where: Grant Park, Chicago, plus four citywide districts
  • Park sessions: Morning 9 AM–1 PM CST or Afternoon 2 PM–6 PM CST
  • Headliners: Zeraora debut, Mega Mewtwo via Super Mega Raids, Blaze Breed Tauros (Chicago-exclusive)
  • Tickets: Starting at $33 per day, available while supplies last
  • Estimated economic impact: $1 million for the City of Chicago

If you missed out on tickets, don’t worry — there’s still plenty of action accessible across the city, and a global Twitch broadcast brings the festival to anyone with a Wi-Fi connection.

item.title: Oracle's Stunning AI Pivot: 30,000 Layoffs Meet $50B Bet
item.description:
Imagine posting your best quarter ever — and laying off 30,000 people the same month. That is exactly what Oracle is doing right now, and Wall Street can’t decide whether to cheer or flinch.

Quick Summary: Oracle is finalizing the departure of roughly 30,000 employees (about 18% of its global workforce) between June 1 and June 15, 2026. The cuts come despite 22% revenue growth to $17.2 billion last quarter, 44% cloud revenue growth, and a staggering 243% jump in its AI segment. Oracle has committed approximately $50 billion in capital expenditure for fiscal 2026, much of it aimed at AI data centers — including a new Michigan campus with OpenAI under the Stargate venture.

item.title: TradingView Ultimate Guide: Essential Features Powering 2026 Markets
item.description:
TradingView Ultimate Guide: Essential Features Powering 2026 Markets

What if a single browser tab could replace your Bloomberg terminal, your news feed, and your charting software — all at once? For millions of traders, that tab is already open, and it says TradingView at the top.

Once known as a niche tool for chart enthusiasts, TradingView has become one of the most quietly powerful forces in retail finance. Its 2026 upgrades, from Fibonacci-level alerts to deeper exchange integrations, are pushing it from “a charting site” into something closer to a full-stack market workstation.

item.title: Earthquake Now: Essential Real-Time Tracking Guide
item.description:
Did the ground just move under you — or did you imagine it? Within the last 72 hours, multiple earthquakes have rattled communities from the San Francisco Bay Area to northern Japan, and the question “earthquake now?” is trending across search engines for good reason.

Quick Summary: A magnitude 6.1 quake struck northern Japan on April 27. The New Madrid Seismic Zone produced a magnitude 4.0 event on April 24 felt across four U.S. states. California saw two minor quakes near Daly City and a 3.4 near Cabazon. Real-time tracking through the USGS and EMSC is the fastest way to confirm what you just felt.

item.title: SpaceX Launch Surge: 600 Landings and a Starlink Blitz
item.description:
Here’s a number that would have sounded like science fiction a decade ago: 600 rocket landings. That’s what SpaceX quietly crossed this week, even as its Falcon 9 fleet closed out one era and prepared to open another.

Key Takeaways

  • SpaceX hit 600 successful booster landings during a Sunday Starlink mission.
  • The final GPS III satellite launched for the U.S. Space Force on April 21, 2026.
  • A Vandenberg Falcon 9 is set to deliver 25 more Starlink satellites to low Earth orbit.
  • SpaceX is preparing its 12th Starship flight, a key step toward returning humans to the Moon.
  • Rival Blue Origin’s New Glenn rocket is grounded after a satellite deployment mishap.

The SpaceX launch tempo in April 2026 is not just busy. It is reshaping the economics of getting to orbit, and it is doing it while a major competitor sits on the sidelines.

item.title: Cloud Computing in 2026: The Surprising Shift Reshaping Enterprise Infrastructure
item.description:
Did you know that 93% of enterprises are now pulling their AI data back from public cloud providers? In 2026, the cloud computing landscape looks radically different from even two years ago — and the forces driving this transformation go far beyond simple cost optimization.

Key Takeaways

  • Global cloud spending reached $110 billion in Q4 2025 alone, fueled by AI infrastructure investments
  • The “borderless cloud” era is ending as sovereign computing requirements surge worldwide
  • Specialized AI cloud providers (neoclouds) are emerging as serious competitors to hyperscalers
  • CoreWeave signed a major AI cloud agreement with Anthropic, signaling a shift in compute partnerships
  • Most enterprises now favor hybrid infrastructure models as they balance AI ambitions with data control

Cloud Spending Hits Record Highs — But the Money Is Going Somewhere New

The numbers are staggering. Global cloud spend reached $110 billion in the final quarter of 2025, according to an Omdia report, with AI infrastructure investments driving the lion’s share of that growth. But look closer, and you’ll see the spending patterns have fundamentally shifted.

item.title: SpaceX Launch Schedule April 2026: Starship Delays, Starlink Missions, and What's Next
item.description:
SpaceX is juggling an unprecedented launch cadence in April 2026 — firing off Falcon 9 rockets nearly every other day while quietly pushing back its most ambitious Starship test yet. Meanwhile, NASA’s Artemis II crew is circling the Moon for the first time since 1972, and China’s attempt to rival Falcon 9 just ended in failure.

Here’s everything happening in the world of SpaceX launches right now.

Key Takeaways

  • SpaceX delayed the next Starship test launch by a month, according to Elon Musk
  • Multiple Falcon 9 Starlink missions are scheduled from both coasts throughout April
  • Artemis II launched successfully, sending astronauts on a historic Moon flyby
  • SpaceX won a $178.5 million Space Force contract for missile tracking satellites
  • China’s heavyweight rocket designed to challenge Falcon 9 failed on launch

SpaceX Starship Test Pushed Back — What Happened?

The biggest SpaceX news this week isn’t a launch — it’s a delay. SpaceX has pushed back its crucial Starship test launch by approximately one month, Elon Musk confirmed on April 3, 2026.

item.title: Crypto ATM Scams Cost Americans $333 Million — What You Need to Know
item.description:
Did you know the average victim of a crypto ATM scam is 73 years old and loses roughly $17,000 in a single transaction? That’s not a hypothetical — it’s a real statistic from fraud investigators in Manchester, New Hampshire, and it’s part of a national crisis that’s finally forcing lawmakers to act.

Key Takeaways:

  • The FBI reported $333.5 million in crypto ATM scam losses from January to November 2025 — up from $250 million in 2024.
  • Indiana became the first state to ban crypto kiosks outright, sidelining roughly 800 machines.
  • The global crypto ATM count has dropped to 38,928 after a net loss of 597 machines in Q1 2026.
  • New Hampshire, West Virginia, and Arizona are advancing new consumer protection legislation.

Crypto ATM Fraud Is Surging Across the United States

The numbers are staggering. According to the FBI, fraudsters stole $333.5 million from Americans through bitcoin ATM scams between January and November 2025. That figure represents a 33% increase over the roughly $250 million lost in 2024, which itself was more than double the previous year’s total.

item.title: iPhone Apple 2026: Foldable Launch, DarkSword Spyware Alert, and the Roadmap Ahead
item.description:
iPhone Apple News: A Week That Changed Everything

Apple just dropped one of the most revealing weeks in iPhone history — and most people missed the biggest story buried in the headlines.

Between a spyware campaign targeting hundreds of millions of devices, leaked roadmaps pointing to a foldable iPhone arriving as early as December 2026, and a fierce legal battle over the future of the iPhone camera, this is a pivotal moment for anyone who owns or plans to buy an iPhone.
